# 8.css consolidated reference

8.css is a CSS-only UI library inspired by Windows 8 Start Screen / Modern UI and Windows 8 desktop. It is strongly inspired by 7.css by khang-nd in its semantic HTML approach, component-by-component docs, live previews, and copyable snippets. The initial code came from SamWanekeya/Windows-8-Metro-UI, an old Start Screen experiment with no new commits recorded after June 2017. The project was forked to evolve the prototype into a reusable library. The inherited MIT license is preserved. 8.css is not an official Microsoft product and is not endorsed by the 7.css author.

## Source of truth
- Edit component modules in gui/.
- Run npm run build to regenerate src/8.css, dist/8.css, and dist/gui/*.css.
- Do not hand-edit generated CSS.
- Keep README.md, docs/index.html, docs/components.md, AGENTS.md, llms.txt, and this file synchronized.
- Runtime package must stay CSS-only.

## Module order
base.css, tiles.css, buttons.css, forms.css, feedback.css, window.css, app-bar.css, dialog.css, responsive.css. The complete dist/8.css bundle combines modules in that order. For modular use, import dist/gui/base.css first, then one or more component modules.

## Installation target
The planned public package name is 8.css. It has not been published yet, and the unscoped name must be checked before release. Once published, install with npm install 8.css and import 8.css/dist/8.css. For plain HTML, use https://unpkg.com/8.css/dist/8.css. Prefer exact version pins in production.

## Public API
Start Screen: .w8-start-screen, .w8-start-heading, .w8-start-subtitle, .w8-tiles.
Tiles: .w8-tile, .w8-tile__symbol, .w8-tile__label, .w8-tile__meta, .w8-tile__count; size modifiers .w8-tile--wide, .w8-tile--tall, .w8-tile--large; colors .w8-tile--blue, .w8-tile--cyan, .w8-tile--purple, .w8-tile--magenta, .w8-tile--green, .w8-tile--orange, .w8-tile--red, .w8-tile--dark.
Buttons: .w8-button, .w8-button--primary, .w8-button--subtle.
Fields: .w8-input, .w8-select, .w8-textarea, .w8-field, .w8-label, .w8-help.
Choices: .w8-check, .w8-radio, .w8-choice, .w8-toggle, .w8-toggle__input.
Feedback: .w8-progress, .w8-badge, .w8-badge--blue, .w8-notice variants, .w8-divider.
Tabs: .w8-tabs, .w8-tab.
Desktop: .w8-window, .w8-title-bar, .w8-title-bar__text, .w8-title-bar__controls, .w8-window-control, .w8-window-control--close, .w8-window-body, .w8-window-footer.
App bar and dialog: .w8-app-bar, .w8-app-bar__item, .w8-dialog, .w8-dialog__body, .w8-dialog__footer.

## Accessibility boundary
Use semantic HTML and accessible names. Keep focus visible. Check contrast with custom colors. Test narrow viewports and reduced-motion settings. CSS styles controls but does not manage application state, tab keyboard navigation, window controls, announcements, or focus management.

## Validation
Run npm run build, npm test, and npm run build:site. Tests check module/bundle parity, expected selectors, absence of CSS imports, and balanced CSS braces. These are lightweight checks, not a full CSS parser or browser test suite.
